clue.text: Ancient pursuit Olympic hosts discover after tea

parts.note: cha = tea, a colloquial British word from Chinese
Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Olympic Games
to trace = to track down, discover

explanation.surface: Some sport the Olympic hosts have dug up, found over a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympic hosts' reads as a committee; it is one host city, RIO. 'Pursuit' is a pastime here, not a chase, though a chariot race is both.
explanation.definitionFit: Chariot racing was a sport of ancient Greece and Rome, so it is an ancient pursuit.

clue.text: Bag that's antique found in auditorium

indicators.note: the antique is found inside the auditorium

explanation.surface: A vintage bag left behind in a concert hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found in' is the container signal; 'antique' is a plain synonym and says nothing about the bag's age.
explanation.definitionFit: A holdall is a large soft travelling bag.

clue.text: Swimmer ran, seldom swimming!

indicators.note: letters that swim about are moving out of order

explanation.surface: A swimmer who ran rarely and swam instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' looks like the athlete in the surface; it is a fish, and 'swimming' tidily tells you what to do with the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The red salmon, or sockeye, is a Pacific fish, and any fish is a swimmer.

clue.text: Exercise in dictionary selected

indicators.note: the exercise goes inside the dictionary

explanation.surface: Someone chose to do a drill in the dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: The dictionary is the Oxford one, always abbreviated in crosswords; the exercise is school physical training.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to choose, so opted means selected.

clue.text: Edited series about university put out again

indicators.note: text that has been edited has been rearranged
the rearranged series goes around the university

explanation.surface: A university's book series revised and published a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole of 'series' is rearranged, and the U is tucked in near the end of the new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a publisher who brings an out-of-print title back is issuing it a second time.

clue.text: Sassy in the past, musical

explanation.surface: A show that once had attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sassy' in its American sense of smart and stylish gives CHIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is the Kander and Ebb stage musical, later a film.

clue.text: Author only present in spirit?

definitions.meaning: a ghost is a spirit; this writer is unseen, with someone else's name on the cover

explanation.surface: A writer who is there in spirit only, like a dead author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In spirit' sounds like the phrase for someone absent who supports you; read literally, the author is a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghostwriter writes a book published under another person's name, so is present in the work but invisible.

clue.text: Otherwise hopeless loser, first in effect

indicators.note: a hopeless effort is a mess, so the letters are scrambled
takes only the first letter of 'effect'

explanation.surface: A hopeless loser, who is in effect first after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hopeless loser' reads as one insult; 'hopeless' is working on 'loser'.
explanation.definitionFit: Or else means otherwise, as in 'hurry, or else you'll miss it'.

clue.text: Injured, ran — ran fast!

parts.note: to run a company is to lead it, so ran = led

explanation.surface: An injured runner who still sped off.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'ran' means managed, giving LED; the second belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurtle is to move at great speed, so hurtled means ran fast.

clue.text: One proposal finally grasped by ignoramus — seen late in the day?

indicators.note: to be grasped by something is to be held within it, so these letters go inside the ignoramus

parts.note: a twit is a foolish, ignorant person

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of proposal

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dimwit is handed a single proposal and finally gets it, but only at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of proposal and the numeral I go together inside TWIT. The question mark marks a definition by description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilit describes things lit by twilight, the dim light at dusk, so things seen as evening falls.

clue.text: Earner — of a crust?

definitions.meaning: the person who brings the money in
earning a crust is British slang for making a living; read literally, the crust is on a loaf

explanation.surface: Someone who works to put food on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earn a crust' is British for make a living. The dash splits the phrase so that the crust becomes real bread, won by the earner.
explanation.definitionFit: A breadwinner is the person whose earnings support a household.

clue.text: Something like a 21 Down for queen

definitions.meaning: 21 Down is a dried grape; this is one of the same family, paler and seedless
the wife of an Eastern ruler

explanation.surface: A dried fruit chosen for a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Solve 21 Down first: RAISIN points straight to the dried-fruit sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultana is a dried seedless grape much like a raisin, and also the wife of a sultan, his queen.

clue.text: Wretchedness in spinning of a spider

indicators.note: the spinning of letters sets them turning into a new order, fitting a spider at work on its web

parts.note: taken as written: its seven letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A gloomy observation that there is misery in the way a spider spins its web.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinning' looks like the spider's own activity, but it is what reorders the letters of 'a spider'.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is a state of hopeless misery, the same as wretchedness.

clue.text: Back on head in wig, roller?

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another comes after it, so the back part follows
the head of a word is its first letter, here the first letter of wig

parts.note: the heel is the back part of the foot or of a shoe

explanation.surface: A puzzled note about a hair roller placed at the back of the head under a wig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' is not an instruction to reverse: it is the heel. The question mark flags a definition by example, since a wheel is one thing that rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel is a thing that rolls, so it can be called a roller in a whimsical, descriptive sense.

clue.text: Boozer prods me, drunk, a state

indicators.note: the pub pokes into ME, ending up inside it

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub

explanation.surface: A drunk poking the speaker, one of those states people get in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' looks like the drunk; it is British slang for a pub, and 'drunk' is a noun here. 'Prods' works as an insertion, the pub poking into the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the clue says only 'state', and this is one of the fifty US states, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Latest hack pens fine report

parts.note: F = fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: The latest journalist writes a good report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' and 'pens' conjure a journalist writing; hack is the verb slash, and pens means encloses. F goes into SLASH after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsflash is a brief urgent news report.

clue.text: Switched on, we think?

definitions.meaning: the question mark hints that this is only our flattering opinion of ourselves

explanation.surface: We like to think we are clued up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switched on' reads as a light or machine; it is the slang for alert and informed.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: switched on means alert and well informed, which is what having inside knowledge makes you.

clue.text: City pal's novel, classic

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A friend in the City has written a novel that is a classic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' and 'classic' both look like books; novel is the adjective new, and classic means typical, as in a classic mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Classic can mean typical of its kind: a classic example is a typical one.

clue.text: Teams in heart of Mexico — and Marxists?

definitions.meaning: sides of eleven players, as in football or cricket
look at the centre of the word MEXICO: two letters that make a Roman numeral
likewise the centre of MARXISTS: the same numeral with a plural S

explanation.surface: Teams of revolutionaries in the heart of Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: A team of eleven is written XI, and XI sits at the centre of MEXICO while XIS sits at the centre of MARXISTS. Nothing in the clue is taken to build the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Football and cricket teams are called elevens, as they have eleven players.

clue.text: Fixer, cheat

definitions.meaning: a small threaded fastener that holds things together
as a verb, to swindle someone out of money

explanation.surface: A match-fixer who cheats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixer' suggests a crooked go-between; here it is hardware.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw is a fastener, and to screw someone out of money is to cheat them.

clue.text: Model notices hunk

indicators.note: to model clay is to reshape it

explanation.surface: A model spots a handsome man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' and 'hunk' paint a fashion shoot; model is a verb working on NOTICES, and hunk means a chunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunk is a large piece cut off something, a section.

clue.text: Something shrivelled up is observed in shower

indicators.note: the IS is seen inside the shower

explanation.surface: Something that has shrivelled up is spotted in the shower.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests skin wrinkled by a long shower; the shower is weather here, not a bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a grape dried in the sun shrinks and wrinkles, so it is something shrivelled up.

clue.text: A retired reporter, say

parts.note: an ex- is a former one, retired

explanation.surface: A retired journalist, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example'; it is the verb, and a retired reporter is an ex-press man.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: putting a feeling into words is both saying it and expressing it.

clue.text: Capitals in South America modelled on African country

indicators.note: capitals are capital letters: take the first letter of each word

parts.note: first letters of South America Modelled On African

explanation.surface: Capital cities in South America designed along African lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capitals' looks like cities; it means capital letters. The African country is a red herring: Samoa is in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Samoa is an island country in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Female fighting breakaway group

explanation.surface: Women fighting in a splinter group.
explanation.walkthrough: F is the standard abbreviation for female.
explanation.definitionFit: A faction is a dissenting group within a larger body, often one that splits away.

clue.text: Ending in tears, best laugh

explanation.surface: Laughing until you cry is the best laugh of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ending in tears' reads as going wrong; it is just the S. A scream is a very funny thing, as in 'he's a scream'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scream is informal for something hilarious, a real laugh.

clue.text: Silly, like yours truly, primary school age?

parts.note: a child at primary school might be nine years old

explanation.surface: Being as silly as a primary school child, the speaker admits.
explanation.walkthrough: Primary school is for children of about five to eleven, so nine is an example age, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means extremely foolish, like an ass.

clue.text: Rag absorbing water, also within reach

parts.note: a rag is a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A rag that soaks up water, kept handy too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absorbing' suits a rag so well in the surface that the container signal is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close at hand is near enough to reach.
